audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer stated the range comparison: Dredge Line is 1150, while Mel's Radiant Volley is 950 and Solar Snare is 1000.
audit.why: This is the fact the whole lane turns on and it inverts the standard poke-mage instinct. There is no distance from which Mel can throw a spell and still be outside hook range — every time she casts, she is inside it. 'Sit at max 550 range', which the content layer already advises, is only true while she is doing nothing.
audit.corrected: His 1150-range hook out-ranges every spell you own — you are inside it the moment you cast.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers treat Rebuttal as the answer to Dredge Line ('Hold W to eat his Q hook', 'Wait out your W cooldown, then hook') without giving the cooldowns.
audit.why: Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26. Dredge Line is 14/13/12/11/10. At rank 1 that is roughly one covered hook in three, and the ratio never gets better than 26 against 10. Telling a player to hold W for the hook without that ratio makes them believe they are covered when they are not.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal does return Dredge Line, but at 38s against a 14s hook it covers one attempt in three.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags that the matchup never names a single Nautilus ability — the text says 'Q hook', 'passive root', 'E AOE', 'R knockup' throughout.
audit.why: The loading screen is the last moment a player can attach a name to a threat. 'Staggering Blow roots on his first auto' is actionable; 'his autos apply a passive root' is not, because the player cannot look it up or call it in voice.
audit.corrected: Named Staggering Blow, Dredge Line, Titan's Wrath, Riptide and Depth Charge across spikes, wants.foe, whys and the early text.

audit.whatIsWrong: Titan's Wrath appears nowhere in either layer as a burst-absorber.
audit.why: It is a 12s flat-cooldown shield. Mel's whole kill pattern is a stacked Overwhelm detonation, and spending it into a fresh Titan's Wrath wastes the one window the lane offers. Forcing the shield out first is a sequencing rule, not a flavour note.
audit.corrected: Titan's Wrath is a 12s shield that swallows the volley — force it out before you spend a rotation.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer calls this EVEN, 5.5/10, with the tldr 'Free stacking lane — every Q volley builds your execute while he farms politely', and every phase from level 2 onward marked 'Skill'.
audit.why: 35.48% over 31 games is the largest sample in this slice and the content layer's own chart gives Nautilus levels 4-5 onward. 'Free stacking lane' is the single most misleading line in the matchup.
audit.corrected: HARD, 7.5/10, carry threat 7/10; phases Skill / Mel / Skill / Nautilus x4.
sources: scratchpad packet mel.json entry nautilus (winRate 35.48, games 31, levelChart)

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing mentions that Dredge Line pulls Nautilus to terrain, only that it pulls Mel to him.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus towards it.' That is how he arrives from an angle Mel is not watching and how he closes after a gank starts, which matters for a champion whose only stated plan is 'never give him a flat path'. A flat path is not the only path.
audit.corrected: Left as a note rather than an edit — see notes.

edits.before: At Level 1 it's even — one ability each, just trade Q chips and respect that his autos apply a passive root. Level 2 is your single best window: Q poke plus Solar Snare's root lets you land a guaranteed punish when he steps up to last-hit, so play for that. But once his W is up the lane tilts — hold your W to eat his Q hook (it destroys the projectile and fires it back as your damage), because if you waste it he hooks you, roots you on the next auto, and you have no dash to leave. Never stand on a straight line into him with W down.
edits.after: At Level 1 it's even — one ability each, just trade Q chips and respect that Staggering Blow roots on his first auto. Level 2 is your single best window: Q poke plus Solar Snare's root lets you land a guaranteed punish when he steps up to last-hit, so play for that. But once Titan's Wrath is up the lane tilts — Rebuttal does return Dredge Line, yet at 38s against his 14s hook it only ever covers one attempt in three. Never stand on a straight line into him, because his 1150-range hook out-ranges every spell you own.

I did not write anything about Rebuttal reflecting or blocking Depth Charge, because whether a ground-travelling shockwave counts as a reflectable projectile is not answerable from the kit file and getting it wrong would be fatal advice.
